results.label: yes
results.reason: elections_process/national: EC's authority on citizenship scrutiny and electoral roll revision.

notes.subject: polity
notes.why_in_news: The Election Commission of India (ECI) submitted an affidavit to the Supreme Court arguing that the Centre's exclusive power to scrutinize citizenship is limited to cases of voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship
notes.fact_box: The ECI cited Section 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, which allows the Centre to determine when/how an Indian citizen acquired foreign citizenship. The ECI asserted its authority to assess citizenship for electoral roll registration flows from Articles 324 and 326 of the Constitution.

prelims_pointers.text: Article 324: Empowers the Election Commission to supervise and control the conduct of elections.
Article 326: Establishes Indian citizenship as a constitutional precondition for entry into the voter list.
Section 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955: Vests authority in the Centre to determine the termination of citizenship due to voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship.
The ECI submitted a 184-page affidavit in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) case.

notes.mains_question: Examine the constitutional balance between the Election Commission's plenary powers under Article 324 and the Union Government's exclusive jurisdiction over citizenship matters.
mains_dimensions: Constitutional conflict: Reconciling ECI's supervisory mandate under Article 324 with the Centre's exclusive jurisdiction over citizenship status.
Jurisdictional limits: Distinction between 'scrutiny for electoral eligibility' versus 'determination of citizenship' under the Citizenship Act, 1955.
Legislative supremacy: The extent to which parliamentary laws can oust the ECI's constitutional jurisdiction over voter list integrity.

notes.subject: ir
notes.why_in_news: The Ministry of External Affairs announced that President Vladimir Putin will visit India from 4 to 5 December 2025 for the India-Russia Annual Summit.
notes.fact_box: President Vladimir Putin will attend the twenty-third India-Russia Annual Summit at the invitation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The visit aims to review progress in bilateral projects including defence, space, energy, and trade cooperation.

prelims_pointers.text: Putin's visit to India is scheduled for 4 to 5 December 2025.
The visit marks the twenty-third India-Russia Annual Summit.
Vladimir Putin became Acting President of Russia on 31 December 1999 and was formally sworn in on 7 May 2000.
The summit will review progress in defence, space, energy, and trade cooperation.

notes.mains_question: Discuss the evolution of the 'Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership' between India and Russia in the context of contemporary global security challenges.
mains_dimensions: Strategic continuity: Maintaining diplomatic alignment despite changing global conditions and limited high-level meetings.
Sectoral cooperation: Leveraging bilateral projects in defence, space, and energy to bolster mutual strategic interests.
